The other, the one I subscribe to, is that, when the weapon fired and damaged the installation, the portal became unstable, thus ripping the ship in half and sending the two halves on different courses.

In that game, the creator has no knowledge of the special forces program, only that someone has created soldiers without her knowledge. In her journal, the creator is absolutely furious after meeting with the team, and has no idea who created them. In a later story, we get a moment where the creator realizes that the team were likely from that program. I think the thing that most people don't realize is that meeting these soldiers doesn't mean the creator suddenly knows the program exists. She discovered soldiers that aren't her's, that's all. They're never identified by that specific program name. For all she knows, they could be a different class made without her knowledge. And the reason she doesn't seem to react is two fold: 1. By the time we, the player, enter the scene the creator had already been discussing things with other members of the team, so any reaction would have passed (other than her saying "hi" to one member) 2. The creator is smart enough not to ask questions openly, especially when she's in a secure facility. Doing so would get her nowhere at best, in trouble at worst.

Spartan-1's, or ORION candidates, did not have specialized armor. Spartan-IIs were the first to wear powered suits, the Mjolnir Mk. IV platform. This was built on top of the progress makes with the Mk. I-III exosuits, though much of the designs for Mjolnir had to be taken back to the drawing board. The original Mk. IV was a powered assault armor that was environmentally sealed with 90 minutes of emergency oxygen, featured a heads up display with multiple visor settings, and enhanced the strength, speed, and dexterity of the user. Over the course of its operational history, multiple variants released for specialized tasks and combat roles. When it first released, there were a number of designs (hence why we see that Mk. VI looking one in a related production), but the final production model released in the mid-2530s resembled the version seen in a related game. In November of 2551, a version of Mk. V was rolled out for select Spartan teams.  This was very similar to the Mk. IV, but featured energy shields. In August of 2552, the final model of Mk. V was rolled out and given to the surviving Spartan-IIs, just prior to a specific operation. Along with shielding, this version could also carry an AI. A couple months later, Mk. VI was rolled out. This version featured all the upgrades of the Mk. V, but further enhanced a Spartan's abilities and featured integrated biofoam injectors, so medpacks were no longer necessary in the case of severe bodily damage. Around this time, early version of what would become GEN2 suits were rolled out, primarily used by specific Spartans. Spartan-IIIs generally used SPI Armor. This was little more than advanced ODST armor. It offered minimal physiological enhancement and less protection, but also featured photo-reactive plating (ie stealth systems). There were a couple main-line interations of SPI, the second improving the stealth system. Some Spartan-IIIs were pulled from the company, such as the members of Noble Team, placed in special teams, and given Mjolnir armor. With the advent of the Spartan-IVs came Mjolnir GEN2, which dropped the Mark system of GEN1 in favor of progressive updates (basically why GEN2 suddenly has integrated thrusters in a later game). By 2558, most Spartans, be they IIs, IIIs, or IVs, had upgraded to GEN2, though there were a few exceptions: - Some Spartan-IIIs, notably from Gamma Company, continue to use SPI armor. - A specific Spartan, one of the few surviving Spartan-IIs, uses the only known suit of Mk. VII - Specific Spartan Teams use Mk. IV, as both are still out of contact with the UNSC.
